title: Route alias inheritance causes per-key quota amortization to double during rapid alias swaps
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observed credits being amortized twice for some requests immediately after a route alias switch. The behavior manifests when an org-level quota amortization window overlaps with an on-the-fly route alias swap and concurrent high concurrency of requests against both alias names. The amortization ledger receives two effective 'top-up' entries for the same logical request group, temporarily inflating available credits and allowing a brief burst of silent over-allowance.

Why it matters:
- Customers see transient 'free' allowances and then follow-on chargebacks when reconciles run — confusing for billing and can cause revenue leakage.
- Can trigger downstream failovers as usage spikes hit other capacity tiers.

Reproduction (deterministic-ish):
1. Create a route with alias A bound to service S and a per-key amortization policy (burst_credit_topup window 60s).
2. Start a high-concurrency (200 concurrent) synthetic load against alias A for 30s (tokens small).
3. During the load, switch alias A to alias B (instant alias swap via route alias patch).
4. Continue load for another 60s.
5. Observe ledger entries showing two top-ups: one keyed by (org, origin_route=A) and one keyed by (org, origin_route=B) with the same amortization nonce. This results in 2x available burst credit for that org/key for ~one window.

Evidence / logs (extracted):
- runtime/ledger WARN: amortize_topup id=amort-0x1 org=org-123 route=A nonce=0xabc topup=100 -> committed
- runtime/ledger WARN: amortize_topup id=amort-0x1 org=org-123 route=B nonce=0xabc topup=100 -> committed
- enforcement debug: allowed req id=... reason="amortized_credit=200"

Hypothesis:
- Route alias swap path updates the in-memory policy map but does not atomically move the amortization identity token. Concurrent evaluations for requests routed by old and new alias both compute the same amortization nonce and then write separate ledger entries because writes are keyed by (nonce, route_identifier) which differs for the two aliases. The ledger merge path treats them as distinct top-ups. The underlying bug is a race between alias-update propagation + per-request evaluation + amortization write where the intended amortization should be idempotent per "amortization nonce per org/key" not per route alias.

Temporary mitigation (applied 2026-03-11):
- Feature-flagged server-side debounce on route-alias updates: alias updates now have a 2s soft-quiesce that returns a "changing" tag to evaluators which makes amortization a no-op for requests that indicate transient alias state. Deployed to runtime-unstable only. This reduces incidence but is not a correct long-term fix.

Proposed long-term fixes:
1) Canonical amortization key: switch ledger key from (nonce, route_identifier) -> (nonce, org_id, amortization_scope) where amortization_scope is canonicalized across alias swaps (alias -> primary_route_id). This requires route metadata to include a stable primary id that survives alias changes.
2) Make amortize_topup a compare-and-set (apply-if-not-seen) by recording a canonical amortization fingerprint and returning the committed value if seen. This is idempotent even when writes race.
3) Add unit + stress test for alias-swap race: synthetic harness that swaps aliases while hammering evaluators with deterministic nonces to assert only one committed top-up seen for a nonce.

Testing plan:
- Unit: ledger idempotency test, canonical-key derivation tests.
- Integration: run alias-swap stress harness across staging for 8h at 500 RPS with alias rotations every 10s.
- Canary: deploy to runtime-canary with feature-flag enabled for 24h and monitor amortization-count-per-nonce metric.

Rollout plan:
- Merge PR to runtime with feature flag off.
- Run integration harness in staging; iterate on fixes.
- Enable feature flag in canary, then gradual rollout to 10% then 50% then 100% if metrics clean.

Observability changes required:
- Emit amortization_fingerprint metric with labels {org, canonical_route, nonce, succeeded}.
- Add an alert if amortization_fingerprint_count > 1 for same nonce within 5m window.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should canonical_route be the route_id or a separate immutable "alias_parent_id"? Immutable parent simplifies logic but requires migration for older routes.
- CAS vs single-writer lease: CAS is simpler for correctness, but may add contention — needs benchmarking.

References:
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/usage/amortization-ops
- Staging harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-stability/tree/main/alias-swap-harness
